title: Inverse Galois Problem: Non-Solvable Frontier
description: Explores the boundary between solvable and non-solvable realms in the Inverse Galois Problem. Proves the complete characterization: Sn is solvable iff n <= 4. Shows A5 is simple, perfect, and not solvable. Establishes Galois-theoretic fixed field degree formulas. States the full Inverse Galois Conjecture.

meta.author: Lean Genius Research
prerequisites: Galois theory (Galois groups, splitting fields, fixed fields)
Group theory (symmetric groups, alternating groups, solvability, simplicity)
meta.assumptions: 0 axiom declarations. 3 sorry(s): 2 census sorries (A5/S5 realization requires importing other files), 1 intentional sorry for the open Inverse Galois Conjecture.

leanFile.note: Key results: sn_solvable_iff (Sn solvable iff n<=4), a5_simple, a5_commutator_eq_top (A5 is perfect), finrank_over_fixed_field ([K:K^H]=|H|), finrank_fixed_field_over_base ([K^H:F]=[G:H]), cayley_card (Cayley embedding), inverse_galois_conjecture (open problem). Census of 18+ explicitly realized groups.

keyInsights: The solvability divide at n=5 is the fundamental boundary: for n<=4 all symmetric groups are solvable (covered by Shafarevich), for n>=5 they are not
A5 is the smallest non-abelian simple group and the key obstruction to solvability of Sn for n>=5
A5 is perfect ([A5,A5]=A5) - its commutator subgroup equals itself, so the derived series stalls
The Galois correspondence gives [K:K^H]=|H| and [K^H:F]=[G:H] for any subgroup H of Gal(K/F)
Every finite group embeds into a symmetric group (Cayley), connecting IGP to Sn realizability
